summary: LIGGGHTS_USE_SOA_NVE makes fix nve 5.7x slower in situ (205k atoms: 8.54 +- 0.56 s vs 1.50 +- 0.11 s, paired ratio 5.70 +- 0.42, n=6) and 3.0x on a contact bed; AoS<->SoA copies are 72-91 % of the path; SoA kernels alone are only 10-20 % faster than the whole AoS loop
failure_scenario: Anyone enabling the macro for 'SIMD' gets a slower integrator; DEM decks (nve/sphere) never use it
recommendation: Delete ParticleSoA/soa_ member/sync stubs (S-14); for SIMD use the dbl3_t cast idiom inside nve/sphere

summary: Confirms F-25 by measurement: per-dump wall time of dump hdf5 grows linearly with dump index (0.9-1.0 ms at dump 100 -> 20-27 ms at dump 3000; 64 atoms); 3000 dumps take 42.2 +- 0.1 s vs 0.036 s for dump custom .bin; final XDMF 3.69 MB so ~5.5 GB rewritten; 90 % of CPU samples in libc, 6 % in libhdf5
failure_scenario: Long production run with frequent dumps: output time grows quadratically and eventually dominates the run
recommendation: Append one Grid per dump (seek before closing tags) or write XDMF once at end; keep the HDF5 file open between dumps

summary: dump hdf5 is 11x faster than text dump custom but 1.5-1.8x slower than the existing binary dump custom (.bin): np1 654 vs 990 MB/s, np4 308 vs 541 MB/s (25k atoms, 51 dumps); throughput drops from 1 to 4 ranks (per-dump collective H5Fopen/close + 6 H5Dcreate); HDF5 file carries ~3.8x metadata overhead at small N
failure_scenario: Users switch to HDF5 expecting faster I/O on one node and get slower output than .bin
recommendation: Keep file open, one extendible dataset per field (H5MD layout) instead of one group per step; benchmark on multi-node Lustre before claiming collective-I/O scalability

summary: Micro-optimisations (sqrt avoidance, x[j] hoisting, fix_wall_gran hoisting, checkBin null-check removal, incrementPackedInt) give no measurable whole-run gain vs HEAD: drum loop ratio 0.994 [0.985,1.002], chute 1.020 [0.983,1.057], bed 1.040 [0.92,1.16] (min-ratio 0.988); per-fix wall/gran -3.9 % (drum) vs +6.0 % (chute) (opposite signs); vectorisation reports identical to HEAD
failure_scenario: Report section claiming speed-ups from these changes cannot be substantiated; readers may expect gains
recommendation: Stop micro-optimising scalar paths; keep changes only where they fix bugs (fix_wall_gran latent fix_mesh, checkBin >=nlocal); document as neutral

summary: Profile of the pair-dominated bed: NormalModel<HERTZ>::surfacesIntersect (20-23 %) and TangentialModel<HISTORY>::surfacesIntersect (12 %) are out-of-line calls per contact; pair loop not vectorised in either tree ('two or more consecutive inner loops'; 'statement clobbers memory: sqrt' because -fno-fast-math keeps -fmath-errno)
failure_scenario: Every contact pays two call/return + spills; SIMD impossible
recommendation: Try always_inline on surfacesIntersect and -fno-math-errno (not -ffast-math); accept only with bitwise-identical smoke + measured Pair gain; then OpenMP (S-08)

summary: S-07 measured: with a rebuild EVERY step (worst case, dense 25k bed) history adds +1.6-1.7 ms/build to Neigh (+12-15 %) and +2.4 ms/build in FixContactHistory::pre_exchange; in a normal run (13 builds/2000 steps) the whole transfer is ~0.3-0.5 % of the loop. Not a hotspot; a sorted/hash index is not justified
failure_scenario: None (refutes the evaluation report's ranking of a CSR/hash history index as a cheap high-value win)
recommendation: Keep linear scan; revisit only for Z >> 10 (cohesive/polydisperse) with the S-07 counters

summary: [LEGACY] Static decomposition: on a 200k settled bed filling ~55 % of the box the default processors * * * grid (2x2x2 / 2x2x4) leaves half / 8 of 16 ranks with zero particles (Nlocal max/avg 2.00 / 2.87) -> loop 1.82x (8 ranks) and 2.52x (16 ranks) slower than an x-y grid; identical in HEAD
failure_scenario: Any hopper/silo/chute/settling case run with the default grid wastes 45-60 % of the allocation; time-varying fills cannot be fixed by a hand-picked grid
recommendation: Implement balance/fix balance shift with contact-count weights (S-05); meanwhile document processors * * 1 for beds

summary: Scaling on one shared node (cpus 16-31 = SMT siblings of busy cores): strong 200k speed-up 11.3x on 16 ranks (eff 0.70 mean / 0.59 min-based), weak 12.5k/rank eff 0.84/0.72/0.65/0.49 at 2/4/8/16; Comm 7.5-7.8 % and untimed synchronisation wait ('Other') ~20 % at 16 ranks although Nlocal/Neighs are balanced to 1 %
failure_scenario: Wait time is invisible in the timing breakdown (lands in Other) so users misattribute scaling loss
recommendation: Time the per-step collective separately (add a TIME_SYNC category) and re-run on a dedicated node before any MPI optimisation
